sources.publisher: Prime Minister of the Hellenic Republic
sources.title: Official English biography: education, finance career and political roles
sources.findings: Read the official English biography’s education, private-sector and political-career paragraphs. It identifies Harvard Social Studies, Stanford international relations and Harvard Business School MBA; London investment-banking/consulting, subsequent Greek private-equity work and a three-year NBG Venture Capital CEO tenure. He was not CEO of the entire National Bank of Greece group. The 2003 World Economic Forum distinction is Global Leader for Tomorrow, not an invented different award. It separates late-2003 entry into public life from election the following year. Promotional descriptions of reform success, party transparency and national awards are not independent effectiveness findings. Its compressed 2019/2023 narrative is expanded using the caretaker-government record.

sources.title: Parliamentary biography: exact birth date, degree years and first election
sources.findings: Read the Hellenic Parliament identity, studies and first-election paragraphs. They give Athens, 4 March 1968; Harvard bachelor in Social Studies 1990; Stanford MA in International Relations 1993; Harvard Business School MBA 1995. Do not silently turn Social Studies into a sociology major. The page combines a legacy 17th-term heading with newer navigation and current office/constituency labels; it is not treated as a clean current parliamentary register. It redundantly lists 2004 among re-elections after first election in March 2004; that duplicate is not copied. Exact educational years supersede conflicting foreign-government search excerpts, without claiming original certificate authentication.

sources.publisher: Prime Minister of the Hellenic Republic
sources.title: Greek biography: 2013–2015 ministry, 10 January 2016 leadership and public-service priorities
sources.findings: Read relevant Greek official CV paragraphs: early employers, venture-capital role, Athens B parliamentary service, administrative-reform/e-government ministry from 25 June 2013 to 27 January 2015, party presidency elected 10 January 2016, and gov.gr policy priorities. The paragraph moves from 2016 to first becoming prime minister in July without restating 2019; do not infer July 2016. Its rounded 41% for June 2023 is not reproduced as an exact tally. The claim of over 2000 digital services and unqualified success language are not independently audited; public text mentions the stated expansion without the number.

sources.title: 8 July 2019 actual swearing-in after New Democracy election victory
sources.findings: Read the opening Reuters report dated 8 July 2019 on Investing.com. It confirms actual swearing-in after the previous day’s election, 158 of 300 seats and transition from Alexis Tsipras. Investment, employment and tax pledges are promises at inauguration, not completed outcomes. Immediate market movements and broad assessments of the previous government are not imported. No claim to have reviewed every appointment decree or final election return.

sources.title: 25 May 2023 caretaker appointment of Ioannis Sarmas
sources.findings: Read Reuters’ 25 May 2023 caretaker-government report: Ioannis Sarmas actually took the oath after the 21 May vote failed to produce an outright majority, and the largest parties declined coalition mandates. The next vote would use bonus seats for the leading party. Its 24 May file-photo caption concerns the preceding presidential meeting, not the oath. This source establishes a real interruption of Mitsotakis’s premiership, not merely a vacation or a simultaneous second prime minister.

sources.title: 26 June 2023 swearing-in after repeat election and 158-seat result
sources.findings: Read the actual-inauguration opening of the updated 26 June 2023 Reuters report on Investing.com. New Democracy won 158 of 300 seats on 25 June and Mitsotakis was sworn in on Monday after a caretaker interlude. The URL retains future-tense wording but the read body reports the oath occurred. Plans to raise wages, improve credit ratings and change services are not completed achievements on that date. The 158-seat result is not an increase over 2019’s same number; the difference from May 2023 arises under different electoral rules.

sources.title: 15 February 2024 marriage-equality vote, cross-party support and policy limits
sources.findings: Read Reuters’ 15 February 2024 parliamentary-vote account, updated 16 February. It records 176 supporting MPs out of 300 seats, marriage and adoption rights, dissent or abstention within New Democracy and support from opposition parties. Publication in the official gazette is a later legal step, so the public date is explicitly passage rather than an assumed gazette/commencement date. Assisted-reproduction obstacles and limits on surrogacy were not all removed. The article also records long-running civil-society campaigning; the reform is not attributed solely to one person.

sources.publisher: Prime Minister of the Hellenic Republic
sources.title: 8 August 2022 statement acknowledging wiretap and denying prior knowledge
sources.findings: Read the Greek prime-ministerial statement dated 8 August 2022, especially acknowledgment of EYP interception of Nikos Androulakis, the claim of prosecutorial authorization, denial of prior knowledge and assessment of political unacceptability. These are Mitsotakis’s positions, not independent adjudication of legality or mental state. The page’s modern site-header date is not the statement date. Conventional telephone interception and Predator infection are distinct methods; no unsupported assertion that every target experienced both. The embedded video was not watched.

sources.title: 26 February 2026 convictions of four spyware-linked businesspeople, appeal and further investigation
sources.findings: Read the substantive Reuters 26 February 2026 paragraphs. Four businesspeople linked to Intellexa/related firms were convicted in the spyware case; sentences were pending appeal and the case was referred for possible further investigation. The 2024 prosecutor’s shelving of an EYP case and the government’s denials are historical procedural positions, not proof that every oversight question is settled. No conviction of Mitsotakis personally is established. Numerical sentence totals and actual prison-service claims are omitted; no final appeal decision or original judgment was reviewed.

sources.title: 2 March 2026 assessment of spyware convictions and remaining accountability concerns
sources.findings: Read the relevant 2 March 2026 HRW dispatch: four defendants convicted on 26 February, execution suspended pending appeal, additional investigation requested, and continuing criticism of the failure to establish responsibility for ordering surveillance. The NGO’s accountability assessment is attributed, not a court judgment against the prime minister. Its description of broader state links is not silently converted into a final adjudicated finding. Keep 2 March publication separate from 26 February judgment; do not infer later appeal outcomes.

sources.title: 23 March 2026 opening of Tempi rail-crash trial, defendants and government response
sources.findings: Read the substantive 23 March 2026 Reuters report syndicated by MarketScreener: the 28 February 2023 Tempi collision killed 57, proceedings involving 36 defendants began and were adjourned amid venue problems, and the government denied wrongdoing while promising reform. No politicians were being tried in that opening case; this is not a permanent statement about every separate later proceeding. The public text dates the opening, not a November claim of final verdict. Relatives’ cover-up allegations, investigative findings, criminal charges and political responsibility are distinct. No complete accident investigation or original trial docket was read.

sources.publisher: Prime Minister of the Hellenic Republic
sources.title: 14 November 2026 published Wall Street Journal interview with Gordon Fairclough
sources.findings: Read the opening question-and-answer sections of the 14 November 2026 Wall Street Journal interview reproduced on the official site. It confirms an actual exchange with Gordon Fairclough and identifies Mitsotakis as serving prime minister; topics include debt, investment, wages and affordability. His claims of rapid debt reduction, growth and tax success are not treated as independent statistical verification. The 17 November global page header is not the article publication date; 14 November is publication, not a verified recording day. The original subscription article, full audio and every interview paragraph were not reviewed.
